slides.title: Why we move
slides.notes: Name three benefits of regular activity for body and mood. Notes: learners keep a two-day movement log; young people are commonly advised to aim for about 60 minutes a day, so compare the log with that target.

slides.title: Fitness parts and warm-up
slides.slide: L2 Awareness · Fitness parts and warm-up
slides.notes: Explain the main fitness components and why a warm-up lowers injury risk. Notes: run a five-minute warm-up with pulse raiser, mobility and a rehearsal move; learners name which component each test, such as a sit-and-reach, checks.

slides.title: Training zones and principles
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Training zones and principles
slides.notes: Apply specificity and overload and calculate a target heart-rate zone. Notes: for a 16-year-old, 220 minus age gives 204; 60 to 80 per cent is 122 to 163 beats per minute; learners check the zone against a pulse count.

slides.title: Plan a progressive programme
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Plan a progressive programme
slides.notes: Plan a six-week programme with progressive overload and monitoring. Notes: start at 100 minutes a week and add 10 per cent each week, so week four is 133 minutes; learners write what they would do if soreness lasts over two days.

slides.title: Energy systems and levers
slides.slide: L5 Specialist · Energy systems and levers
slides.notes: Analyse energy systems in sprint and endurance events and calculate speed and lever force. Notes: 100 m in 12.5 s is 8 m per second; an effort arm of 4 cm against a load arm of 32 cm and a load of 5 kg needs 40 kg of effort.

slides.title: Oxygen uptake and adaptation
slides.slide: L6 Advanced · Oxygen uptake and adaptation
slides.notes: Calculate oxygen uptake from cardiac output and evaluate adaptations to training. Notes: heart rate 190 and stroke volume 0.12 L give 22.8 L per minute; with a difference of 0.15, uptake is 3.42 L per minute, or 48.9 mL per kg per minute for 70 kg.

slides.title: Load monitoring and evidence
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Load monitoring and evidence
slides.notes: Create a load-monitoring plan and critique the evidence for injury-risk ratios. Notes: session load is effort rating times minutes, 60 minutes at 7 gives 420; an acute week of 400 against a four-week average of 320 gives a ratio of 1.25; discuss limits.
